body.statement: If \(\mathsf{Check}(\mathsf{Cert})=\mathrm{true}\) for \(\mathsf{Cert}=(S^{\star},v^{\star},\mathcal T)\), then \(S^{\star}\in\mathcal P_k\), the checker has independently recomputed \(\overline W(S^{\star})=v^{\star}\), every feasible panel is covered by a verified root-to-leaf branch, and every leaf with a feasible descendant has verified \(\overline W(I\cup E)\geq v^{\star}\). Monotonicity under adding candidates gives \(\overline W(S)\geq\overline W(I\cup E)\geq v^{\star}\) for every feasible descendant \(S\), so \(\overline W(S^{\star})=v^{\star}=D^{\star}\). Conversely, every rational instance admits such an accepted finite certificate by branching until every path is closed. The certificate supplies neither \(D^{\star}\) nor global optimality; both are derived by the checker.
body.justification: The checker makes a reported causal panel auditable without treating generic exact branch certification as the scientific contribution.
body.gap: CheungGleixnerSteffy2017 and Szeider2026 establish general exact proof-log methodology. This corollary only specializes exhaustive checking to the derived causal width and claims no new generic certification framework.
body.consumer: Regulators or independent statisticians can verify the claimed trial panel with a small exact checker without rerunning the original solver.
